historical_references.reference: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq named his daughter Asma bint Abu Bakr after his sister Asma bint Abdul-Muttalib. She is also known as Asma bint Abi Bakr. According to Islamic tradition, she was the first female to embrace Islam and the first woman to perform the Hajj pilgrimage. She was also known as Umm Ammarah and Umm Aws.
historical_references.time_period: 6th Century CE, during the early Islamic period
historical_references.context: Asma bint Abi Bakr was a prominent figure in early Islamic history as one of the first female converts to Islam and the first woman to perform the Hajj pilgrimage.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Abia' is mentioned in the Quran in Surah Al-Imran (verse 33) in reference to the wife of the Prophet Imran, who was the mother of Maryam (Mary) the mother of 'Isa (Jesus). The name Abia is also mentioned in the Torah (Book of Exodus, Chapter 2) as the name of the sister of Moses and Aaron, and the daughter of Amram and Jochebed.
historical_references.time_period: 6th Century BCE, during the time of Prophet Imran, and 13th Century BCE, during the time of Moses and Aaron
historical_references.context: The name 'Abia' has historical significance in both Islamic and Jewish traditions, as it is mentioned in the Quran as the name of the wife of Prophet Imran and in the Torah as the name of the sister of Moses.
